nodes.name: Ni@C precursor preparation
nodes.procedure: The Ni@C precursor was prepared via a previously published method.[22]
nodes.source_text: The Ni@C precursor was prepared via a previously published method.[22]

nodes.name: I-Ni@C gas-assisted diffusion
nodes.procedure: The I-Ni@C catalyst was synthesized via a simplified gas-assisted thermal diffusion process under a 20% H2/Ar atmosphere at 200°C for 1 h, with the iodine and precursor (Ni@C) being upstream and downstream, respectively. The mass ratio for Ni@C:I2 is 3:1.

unit_operations.name: Thermal diffusion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: simplified gas-assisted thermal diffusion process under a 20% H2/Ar atmosphere at 200°C for 1 h

nodes.source_text: Meanwhile, the I-Ni@C catalyst was synthesized via a simplified gas-assisted thermal diffusion process under a 20% H2/Ar atmosphere at 200°C for 1 h, with the iodine and precursor (Ni@C) being upstream and downstream, respectively. The mass ratio for Ni@C:I2 is 3:1.

nodes.name: Pure carbon extraction
nodes.procedure: Pure carbon was obtained by soaking Ni@C in aqua regia for 2 days to dissolve all the components except for carbon.
nodes.source_text: Pure carbon was obtained by soaking Ni@C in aqua regia for 2 days to dissolve all the components except for carbon.

nodes.name: Pure nickel hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: Pure nickel was synthesized according to an existing hydrothermal method.[68]
nodes.source_text: Pure nickel was synthesized according to an existing hydrothermal method.[68]

nodes.name: I-Ni and I-C iodine introduction
nodes.procedure: For I-C and I-Ni, iodine was introduced in the same way as for I-Ni@C.

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The HER performance of I-Ni@C was measured by using a typical three-electrode electrolyzer in 1.0 M KOH media... linear scan voltammograms (LSVs) were tested at a scan rate of 2 mV/s. The Tafel slopes were further extracted... Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was performed at an overpotential (η) of 200 mV... The double-layer capacitance (C_dl) was fitted from the cyclic voltammetry results at different scanning rates from 10 to 60 mV/s... chronoamperometry (i-t) measurements... 80 h at 20 mA/cm².

nodes.source_text: commercial 20% Pt/C and other reference samples were measured under the same conditions... Tafel slope of I-Ni@C, Ni@C, I-Ni, and 20% Pt/C... the reference samples failed almost completely within 5 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Ni@C and I-Ni@C show only metallic Ni (PDF#04-0850) and carbon peaks with no I-associated phase formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b shows that only metallic Ni (PDF#04-0850) and carbon peaks can be observed in the XRD patterns of Ni@C and I-Ni@C, indicating that no I-associated phase formation occurs during the synthesis process.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM image of I-Ni@C shows lattice spacing of 0.21 nm matching Ni (111) plane and graphitic carbon shell with 0.35 nm interlayer distance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image in Figure 1c shows an I-Ni@C particle with a lattice spacing of 0.21 nm, which matches the (111) plane of metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms iodine atoms are atomically dispersed on the surface of carbon-coated nickel nanoparticles in I-Ni@C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the HAADF-STEM image of I-Ni@C confirms that iodine atoms are atomically dispersed in the surface of carbon-coated nickel nanoparticles (Figure 1e and Figure S5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: I K-edge EXAFS of I-Ni@C shows I-Ni coordination at 2.20 Å and weak I-C peak at 1.72 Å with no I-I coordination at 2.50 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S6 shows the I K-edge EXAFS spectra of R space, which exhibit I-Ni coordination at 2.20Å and a weak characteristic I-C peak near 1.72Å for I-Ni@C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows Ni0, Ni2+, and satellite peaks; iodine enhances Ni2+ proportion with I-Ni showing higher Ni valence state than I-Ni@C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p XPS spectra (Figure S7a,b) show three peaks, Ni0, Ni2+, and satellite peaks... Apparently, the introduced iodine enhances the proportion of Ni2+.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L-edge s-XAS shows higher peak intensity in I-Ni than Ni@C and I-Ni@C; C K-edge shows stronger Ni-carbon shell interaction in I-Ni@C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d shows that the peak intensity of the Ni L-edge s-XAS spectra is higher in I-Ni compared to Ni@C and I-Ni@C.

nodes.characterization_summary: RIXS measurements reveal energy loss ΔE values of 1.6 eV (Ni@C), 1.8 eV (I-Ni@C), and 2.0 eV (I-Ni), indicating d-band center order Ni@C > I-Ni@C > I-Ni with main signal shift to higher incidence energies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Table S3 shows that the ΔE for Ni@C, I-Ni@C, and I-Ni is 1.6, 1.8, and 2.0 eV, respectively. This implies that the d-band center of Ni exhibits the following order: Ni@C > I-Ni@C > I-Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ SR-FTIR shows Ni-H absorption band at ~1700 cm⁻¹ for I-Ni@C with intensity increasing at negative potentials, stronger than Ni@C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3e shows that an observable absorption band appeared for I-Ni@C at a vibration frequency region of ~1700 cm⁻¹ (Ni-H bonding).

nodes.characterization_summary: In 1.0 mbar H₂O, Ni 2p shows increased higher energy peaks irreversibly; I 3d shows increased I-C bond proportion indicating H₂O adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a, with reference to ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) conditions, the proportion of higher energy peaks of Ni 2p XPS spectra increased in a 1.0 mbar H₂O environment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Iodine contents determined as 4.6 wt% in I-Ni@C, 3.2 wt% in I-Ni, and 3.1 wt% in I-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) was used to determine the iodine content in the prepared catalyst, with I-Ni@C, I-Ni, and I-C exhibiting iodine contents of 4.6, 3.2, and 3.1 wt %, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image of I-Ni@C reveals relatively uniform nanoparticle morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S2a shows the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image of I-Ni@C, revealing a relatively uniform nanoparticle morphology.
